content.text:
Silhouette: Horizontal red fox frame carried on two hind legs, barn owl wings in place of the forelegs. Host frame is the red fox, setting the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature combining a red fox and a barn owl. The head is that of the red fox, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear discernible eyes. Details: red fox body and legs with its own dense fur on the face, back, flanks, belly, hips, legs and tail, plain coat with no stripes or spots; from the barn owl, as parts and materials on the red fox's own body, broad wings of layered flight feathers in place of the forelegs, standing on two hind legs, wings sized for flight, and layered contour feathers in its own colors grown from the skin as the red fox's own covering over the shoulders and neck, replacing the red fox's dense fur there and conforming to the red fox's body, sized to the red fox's body and following its contours; every covered part keeps the red fox's own length and shape; the dense fur stops at the covering's edge, and the face, back, flanks, belly, hips, legs and tail keep the red fox's own dense fur; deep keel and heavy flight chest. The covering follows the body's own shape. Bilaterally symmetrical with recognizable limbs and visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly with mild countershading. Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing fox-owl hybrid**
I'm planning a silhouette of a single creature with a red fox body and legs, dense plain fur, and broad barn owl wings replacing the forelegs, with layered flight feathers sized to the fox and contour feathers conforming over the shoulders and neck.
**Composing natural history illustration**
I'm assembling a side three-quarter view of the upright fox-owl hybrid with fox head, feathered shoulders, barn owl wings, and countershaded fur, rendered in a natural history watercolor style on a plain light background.
**Finalizing feathered shoulder details**
I'm confirming the wings are positioned correctly and adding more prominent feathered shoulders to complete the natural history illustration for final delivery.
